name: Web Browser
label: Web Browser
description: Fetch one public http/https URL and return readable page text. In-process Java handler `com.studioquack.nodelibrary.nodes.web.WebBrowserNode` uses java.net.http (TLS always verified, HttpClient.Redirect.NORMAL). HTML→text is regex-only (no Jsoup): strip <script>, <style>, comments, then tags, then collapse whitespace. robots.txt is honored by default via `RobotsTxt` with a process-lifetime per-host cache and fail-open (unreachable robots.txt still allows the page GET). Optional location sets Accept-Language. Use this when you already have a URL; use Web Search when you only have a query. Raw HTML is capped at 2000000 bytes; robots.txt at 524288 bytes. Do not use this node to submit forms, run JavaScript, or read authenticated/cookie-gated pages. robots.txt is respected by default and cannot be silently skipped.
author: 5c8b0d45-1d10-4f2e-844c-2318af96b2fa

ports.name: input
ports.description: URL fetch request delivered as inputVariables.input (or currentNode.inputList targetPortValue=input). REQUIRED field: url. OPTIONAL field: max_chars (overrides the instance configurationParameter max_chars for this call only). The Java handler reads a JSON object; a one-element list is unwrapped. Missing/empty url raises INVALID_INPUT 'url is required.'. Do not put configuration knobs here — those are instance configurationParameters (timeout_seconds, user_agent, respect_robots_txt, location). Example: {"url":"https://example.com/docs","max_chars":8000}.

schema.label: url
schema.description: Absolute URL the Java handler GETs with java.net.http. Purpose: identify the document to fetch (and the URL passed to RobotsTxt.canFetch). REQUIRED. Trimmed. Empty/missing raises INVALID_INPUT 'url is required.'. Accepted schemes: exactly 'http' | 'https' (case-insensitive). Parsed with java.net.URI; a blank/missing host, ftp, file, data, javascript, mailto, or scheme-relative URL raises INVALID_INPUT 'url must be http or https.'. Path, query, port, and userinfo may be included; the fragment is not sent. TLS is always verified. Examples: 'https://example.com/docs', 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robots.txt', 'http://example.org:8080/path?q=1'. Do not pass a search query here — use the Web Search node.

schema.label: max_chars
schema.description: Purpose: cap output.content length after regex HTML stripping so the payload stays bounded. OPTIONAL per-call override of configurationParameter max_chars. Accepted values: positive integers (JSON number or numeric string). When omitted, 0, 0.0, or empty string, the instance config max_chars is used (default 12000). Non-numeric non-empty strings fall back to 12000 (not the config value), matching the Python tool. Content longer than this is cut with String.substring and suffixed with '... [truncated]'. Example: 8000. Example to keep more of a long spec: 20000. This is a payload/DoS bound — do not raise it unbounded. Independent of the 2000000-byte raw-HTML cap on the HTTP body.

ports.name: output
ports.description: Single OUTPUT port. Success status values: 'ok' (page text in content, title set, metadata.content_type/status_code present) or 'blocked_by_robots' (robots.txt disallowed this user-agent+URL; the page was NOT fetched; this is a successful outcome with error 'Fetch disallowed by robots.txt'). Downstream nodes should branch on status for robots denial, not on HTTP 200 of the invoke. Example ok: {"status":"ok","url":"https://example.com/","title":"Example Domain","content":"Example Domain This domain is for use in illustrative examples in documents.","metadata":{"content_type":"text/html; charset=utf-8","status_code":200,"fetched_at":"2026-08-20T18:00:00Z","robots":"allowed"}}. Errors raise a BPMN error for the error boundary event (INVALID_INPUT, AUTH_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, HTTP_<status>, REQUEST_FAILED); secrets are redacted.

schema.label: status
schema.description: Outcome of this invocation. Purpose: tell downstream nodes whether content is trustworthy. EXACT accepted values on success: 'ok' | 'blocked_by_robots'. 'ok' = java.net.http GET returned 2xx, HTML was regex-stripped, content/title populated. 'blocked_by_robots' = RobotsTxt.canFetch returned false; the page GET did not run; this is not an exception. Validation, non-2xx, timeout/IO, and unexpected exceptions raise a BPMN error. Always present on a successful return. Example: 'ok'.

schema.label: url
schema.description: URL associated with the result. Purpose: show what was actually retrieved (redirects) or what was rejected. On status='ok' this is the final URL after HttpClient.Redirect.NORMAL (HttpResult.url). On status='blocked_by_robots' this is the requested URL unchanged. Example: 'https://example.com/page'.

schema.label: title
schema.description:
Page title extracted from the raw HTML (before full-page strip). Purpose: a short label for the fetched document. Algorithm: first ... (case-insensitive, DOTALL), inner HTML regex-stripped; if missing, first

...

stripped; else empty string ''. Present on status='ok'. Absent on blocked_by_robots. Does not decode HTML entities (& stays). Example: 'Example Domain'.

schema.label: content
schema.description: Readable page text produced by the Java regex pipeline (no Jsoup): (1) strip <script>...</script> CASE_INSENSITIVE+DOTALL, (2) strip <style>...</style>, (3) strip <!-- ... -->, (4) strip <[^>]+>, (5) collapse \s+ to a single space and trim. Purpose: give agents page wording without markup or scripts. Truncated to max_chars with suffix '... [truncated]' when longer. Present on status='ok'. Absent on blocked_by_robots. Scripts that never close may leak as text (same as the Python tool). Example: 'Example Domain This domain is for use in illustrative examples...'.

schema.label: metadata
schema.description: Fetch diagnostics object. Purpose: record HTTP and robots outcome without putting HTML in logs. Always present on status='ok' and status='blocked_by_robots'. Always includes robots (see child; EXACT values skipped|allowed|disallowed|unreachable) and fetched_at (ISO-8601 UTC from Instant.now().toString()). On status='ok' also includes content_type and status_code. Includes location when the location config is non-empty (trimmed). Example: {"content_type":"text/html; charset=utf-8","status_code":200,"fetched_at":"2026-08-20T18:00:00Z","robots":"allowed","location":"us"}.

children.label: content_type
children.description: HTTP Content-Type response header of the page GET as returned by java.net.http (first value, may include charset). Purpose: tell callers whether the body was HTML, XHTML, or something else that was still regex-stripped. Present on status='ok'. Absent on blocked_by_robots. Empty string when the origin omitted the header. Examples: 'text/html; charset=utf-8', 'application/xhtml+xml', 'text/plain'.

children.label: status_code
children.description: HTTP status code of the page GET after redirects. Purpose: confirm the origin accepted the request. Present on status='ok' only (non-2xx raises a BPMN error with message 'Web browser HTTP error: HTTP <code> for url: <finalUrl>'). Accepted values: integers 200–299. Example: 200.

children.label: fetched_at
children.description: UTC timestamp when the robots decision or page fetch completed. Purpose: audit when this snapshot was taken. Format: ISO-8601 from Java Instant.now().toString() (e.g. ending in Z). Present on status='ok' and status='blocked_by_robots'. Example: '2026-08-20T18:02:11.123Z'.

children.label: robots
children.description: robots.txt outcome for this host. EXACT values: 'allowed' | 'disallowed' | 'unreachable' | 'skipped'. 'allowed' = robots.txt was fetched and permitted this URL. 'disallowed' = blocked_by_robots (page not fetched). 'unreachable' = robots.txt could not be retrieved (fail-open). 'skipped' = robots.txt was not applied for this fetch and a warning was logged. Example: 'allowed'.

children.label: location
children.description: Echo of configurationParameter location when it was non-empty after trim. Purpose: record which Accept-Language mapping was applied. Same codes as the location config (e.g. 'us', 'tr', 'de', 'gb', 'uk'). Absent when location is empty (no Accept-Language header was sent). Example: 'us'.

configurationParameters.label: Timeout Seconds
configurationParameters.description: Purpose: cap connect and request time for both the robots.txt GET and the page GET (java.net.http HttpClient.connectTimeout and HttpRequest.timeout; WebNodeSupport.send floors at 1 second). Accepted values: positive integers (JSON number or numeric string). Non-numeric/empty/missing falls back to 25. Default: 25. Example: 25. Example for slow origins: 45. Values that are too large stall the sandbox thread; keep under 60 unless the origin is known-slow. Applies independently to each HTTP call (robots.txt and page), not as a shared wall clock.

configurationParameters.label: Default Max Characters
configurationParameters.description: Purpose: default maximum characters of regex-stripped page text when input.max_chars is omitted, 0, or empty. Accepted values: positive integers. Default: 12000. Example: 12000. Example for short summaries: 4000. Input max_chars overrides this per call. Truncation suffix is exactly '... [truncated]'. This is a payload/DoS bound on the OUTPUT object, separate from the 2000000-byte raw HTML cap. 0 in this config is passed through (Python parity) and will truncate any non-empty page to '... [truncated]'.

configurationParameters.label: User Agent
configurationParameters.description: Purpose: HTTP User-Agent sent on the page GET and the robots.txt GET, and passed to RobotsTxt.canFetch (substring match, case-insensitive). Accepted values: any non-empty User-Agent string. Empty/missing uses WebNodeSupport.CHROME_UA. Default: 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'. Example (identify the agent): 'StudioQuack-DuckNodeForge/1.0'. robots.txt rules are user-agent-specific — changing this can change blocked_by_robots outcomes. Never log this value if a caller stuffs a secret into it.
configurationParameters.value: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

configurationParameters.label: Respect robots.txt
configurationParameters.description: Default true: WebBrowserNode fetches and honors robots.txt before the page GET (User-Agent match, 524288-byte cap, TLS verified). Unknown or blank values are treated as true. A fetch that is disallowed returns status='blocked_by_robots' and the page is not retrieved. Unreachable robots.txt is fail-open (metadata.robots='unreachable'). Turning this setting off is an operator decision that is logged as a warning on every fetch; the operator remains responsible for the target site's terms. This library does not instruct operators to disable robots.txt. Example: true.
